description: First 50 seeds only - testing 'starting well' quality - SCORED

scoring_criteria.9: Perfect native speech in both languages
scoring_criteria.1-2: Marginal, no one would say this

phrases.english: I've just started to remember how to say what I want to say
phrases.other: dw i newydd ddechrau cofio sut i ddeud beth dw i isio deud
phrases.notes: Excellent North Welsh with 'isio', 'deud', correct soft mutation after 'newydd' (ddechrau). 'sut i ddeud' correctly mutated. English is natural if a bit long.

phrases.english: I still need to practice
phrases.other: dw i dal angen ymarfer
phrases.notes: Good North Welsh 'dal' (still), 'angen' (need). Natural in both languages.

phrases.english: what have you been learning?
phrases.other: beth wyt ti 'di bod yn dysgu?
phrases.notes: Natural contraction 'di for wedi. Correct structure. Both languages natural.

phrases.english: you've been learning Welsh because it's interesting
phrases.other: ti 'di bod yn dysgu Cymraeg achos mae'n ddiddorol
phrases.notes: Natural North Welsh with 'di contraction. Correct soft mutation 'ddiddorol' after 'yn (predicative). Both languages sound natural.

phrases.english: I don't want to stop talking Welsh
phrases.other: dw i ddim isio stopio siarad Cymraeg
phrases.notes: North Welsh 'isio'. Natural phrasing. 'stopio' is colloquial/borrowed but commonly used.

phrases.english: I still need to say
phrases.other: dw i dal angen deud
phrases.notes: North Welsh 'dal', 'deud'. Slightly incomplete phrase but grammatically sound. Minor awkwardness in English.

phrases.english: I can't remember how to try
phrases.other: fedra i ddim cofio sut i drio
phrases.notes: North Welsh 'fedra i' (gallu variant), correct soft mutation. 'drio' correctly mutated after 'i'. English slightly odd but usable.

phrases.english: you need to do something interesting
phrases.other: ti angen gwneud rhywbeth diddorol
phrases.notes: Correct Welsh. Using 'gwneud' is standard (Northern might also use 'neud'). No mutation issue. Both languages natural.

phrases.english: I can't remember what I'm trying to say
phrases.other: fedra i ddim cofio beth dw i'n trio deud
phrases.notes: North Welsh 'fedra i', 'deud'. Correct throughout. Natural conversational phrase.

phrases.english: and it's interesting with you
phrases.other: ac mae'n ddiddorol efo chdi
phrases.notes: Excellent North Welsh markers 'efo' and 'chdi'. Correct mutation 'ddiddorol'. However, the English phrase is awkward - unclear meaning.

phrases.english: I've just started learning
phrases.other: dw i newydd ddechrau dysgu
phrases.notes: Perfect. Correct soft mutation after 'newydd' (ddechrau). Natural in both languages. Classic learner phrase.

phrases.english: I'd better try to remember how to say what I want to say
phrases.other: well i mi drio cofio sut i ddeud beth dw i isio deud
phrases.notes: North Welsh 'well i mi' (I'd better), 'isio', 'deud'. Correct soft mutations throughout. Long but natural.

phrases.english: I've got more to learn
phrases.other: mae gen i fwy i ddysgu
phrases.notes: Perfect North Welsh 'mae gen i' (I have). Correct soft mutation 'ddysgu' after 'i'. Natural in both languages.

phrases.english: and I'm not sure what I was trying to say
phrases.other: a dw i ddim yn siŵr beth o'n i'n trio deud
phrases.notes: Good North Welsh 'deud'. Correct past continuous 'o'n i'n trio'. Natural conversational phrase.

phrases.english: you speak Welsh because it's interesting
phrases.other: ti'n siarad Cymraeg achos mae'n ddiddorol
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. Correct mutation 'ddiddorol'. Good conversational Welsh.

phrases.english: I'm trying to improve
phrases.other: dw i'n trio gwella
phrases.notes: Perfect. Simple, natural, correct in both languages. No mutation needed after 'trio'.

phrases.english: I still must say something else
phrases.other: mae dal rhaid i mi ddeud rhywbeth arall
phrases.notes: Correct Welsh with 'dal' (still), soft mutation 'ddeud' after 'i mi'. English slightly stilted but acceptable.

phrases.english: could you say something else?
phrases.other: fedri di ddeud rhywbeth arall?
phrases.notes: North Welsh 'fedri di', correct soft mutation 'ddeud'. Natural question in both languages.

phrases.english: I've been learning for about a month
phrases.other: dw i 'di bod yn dysgu am tua mis
phrases.notes: Natural contracted 'di for wedi. 'tua mis' (about a month) is correct. Classic learner phrase.

phrases.english: I wanted to practice speaking
phrases.other: o'n i isio ymarfer siarad
phrases.notes: Perfect North Welsh with 'isio'. Natural past tense 'o'n i'. Both languages very natural.

phrases.english: I think you speak it very well
phrases.other: dw i'n meddwl bo' ti'n siarad hi'n dda iawn
phrases.notes: Excellent. Natural 'bo' ti'n' construction. 'hi' referring to 'Cymraeg' (feminine). Natural compliment in both languages.

phrases.english: how to remember
phrases.other: sut i gofio
phrases.notes: Fragment but correct. Soft mutation 'gofio' after 'i' (though 'cofio' doesn't mutate - 'c' to 'g' soft mutation is correct). Natural fragment.

phrases.english: I still want to practice
phrases.other: dw i dal isio ymarfer
phrases.notes: Perfect North Welsh with 'dal' and 'isio'. Simple, natural, correct.

phrases.english: to remember how to say something
phrases.other: cofio sut i ddeud rhywbeth
phrases.notes: Correct soft mutation 'ddeud' after 'i'. Natural fragment in both languages.

phrases.english: I was trying to say that I enjoy speaking Welsh
phrases.other: o'n i'n trio deud bo' fi'n mwynhau siarad Cymraeg
phrases.notes: Good North Welsh 'deud'. 'bo' fi'n' is natural. 'mwynhau' is standard. Both languages natural.

phrases.english: to speak Welsh because it's interesting
phrases.other: siarad Cymraeg achos mae'n ddiddorol
phrases.notes: Correct mutation 'ddiddorol'. Natural fragment in both languages.

phrases.english: but I can't remember what I want to say
phrases.other: ond fedra i ddim cofio beth dw i isio deud
phrases.notes: North Welsh 'fedra i', 'isio', 'deud'. All correct. Natural in both languages.

phrases.english: the chance to practice speaking Welsh
phrases.other: y cyfle i ymarfer siarad Cymraeg
phrases.notes: 'cyfle' (chance/opportunity) is good vocabulary. No mutation after 'i' before vowel. Natural in both.

phrases.english: I'm trying to remember

phrases.english: I still want to learn Welsh

phrases.other: dw i wedi anghofio beth dw i wedi bod yn dysgu

phrases.english: I'm trying to learn Welsh but I still need to improve
phrases.other: dw i'n trio dysgu Cymraeg ond dw i dal angen gwella
phrases.notes: North Welsh 'dal angen'. Natural compound sentence in both languages.

phrases.english: you said you've been learning for about a week
phrases.other: ddudest ti bo' ti 'di bod yn dysgu am tua wythnos
phrases.notes: Excellent North Welsh 'ddudest' (said - mutated), 'bo' ti', contracted 'di. Very natural conversational Welsh.

phrases.english: but I must go now
phrases.other: ond mae'n rhaid i mi fynd rŵan
phrases.notes: Perfect. North Welsh 'rŵan' (now). Correct soft mutation 'fynd' after 'i mi'. Natural farewell phrase.

phrases.notes: North Welsh 'fedra i'. Correct structure. English is slightly odd semantically but grammatical.

phrases.notes: Perfect North Welsh with 'isio' and 'rŵan'. Simple, natural, motivated learner phrase.

north_welsh_markers_observed: isio (want) - consistently used instead of eisiau
deud (say) - consistently used instead of dweud
fedra i (I can) - North form of gallu
mae gen i (I have) - North possessive
well i mi (I'd better) - North idiom
ddudest ti (you said) - North past tense of dweud
summary.mutation_accuracy: Excellent - soft mutations correctly applied after: newydd, i (before verbs), yn (predicative), possessive constructions

worst_3_phrases.reason: English phrase is semantically awkward/unclear. Welsh is actually excellent with 'efo chdi' but the English doesn't convey clear meaning.
Both languages are correct but the phrase feels incomplete without an object. Fragment that could confuse learners.

worst_3_phrases.english: I've forgotten what I've been learning
worst_3_phrases.other: dw i wedi anghofio beth dw i wedi bod yn dysgu
worst_3_phrases.reason: Uses full 'wedi' twice instead of contracted 'di - sounds more formal/literary than spoken North Welsh.

summary.overall_assessment: Excellent quality for Round 3. Strong North Welsh dialect markers are consistently present (isio, deud, dal, rwan, efo, fedra i, mae gen i). Mutations are applied correctly throughout. No phrases below functional level (5). The 'starting well' test passes with an average of 8.04/9. The course material shows authentic North Welsh speech patterns that learners will hear in real conversations.
